problem_statement: DesignRevision shards-dashboard is a runnable Bootstrap 4 admin dashboard rebranded into Beacon Editorial, a fictional content-operations dashboard for a small newsroom (a Blog Dashboard, a Blog Posts grid, an Add New Post workflow, forms, tables and a user profile) that already ships one coherent design system: a shared left sidebar navigation (nav-link anchors inside aside.main-sidebar), a shared top navbar and page-header pattern, a shared card.card-small pattern used on the dashboard and blog-posts pages, and a shared footer wrapping every page. The newsroom runs an editorial handoff workflow - every bulletin moves through the stages Planning -> In Review -> Scheduled -> Published - but there is no place to see the board and no way to focus on one stage. Add an Editorial Bulletins board at bulletins.html, built from the shared sidebar/top-navbar/footer chrome and the shared card grid, where each bulletin card is tagged with its editorial status, ABOVE a status filter bar that is the board's primary control: a chip row (All / Planning / In Review / Scheduled / Published, each with a live count) and a live readout that reads 'Showing N of 6 | <status>'. Clicking a status chip must actually re-filter the card grid to that status, mark the clicked chip active, and re-sync the readout to the shown subset and the selected status label (for example, clicking In Review shows only the two in-review bulletins and updates the readout to 'Showing 2 of 6 | In Review'). Surface the workflow across the dashboard: an 'Editorial focus' cross-page strip linking to the board must appear on the Blog Dashboard and the Blog Posts operations page as well as on the board itself, and a 'Bulletins' entry must be registered in the shared sidebar navigation of every page. Keep the filter bar, its chip row and the card grid free of horizontal overflow on desktop and at 390px mobile (the chip row must wrap rather than force the page wider than the viewport), keep the chips and readout legible and the cards non-overlapping, and keep the existing dashboard pages intact.
required_content: Add an Editorial Bulletins board at bulletins.html built from the dashboard's shared sidebar/top-navbar/footer chrome and the shared card grid, with six grounded newsroom bulletin cards each tagged with an editorial status (Planning, In Review, Scheduled or Published).

Above the grid, add a status filter bar (the board's native control): an 'Editorial focus' chip row with All / Planning / In Review / Scheduled / Published chips each showing a live count, plus a live readout element reading 'Showing 6 of 6 | All bulletins' initially.

Wire the filter so clicking a status chip marks it active, filters the card grid to only that status, and re-syncs the readout to 'Showing N of 6 | <Status>' for the selected status (clicking In Review yields 'Showing 2 of 6 | In Review' and two visible cards).

Add an 'Editorial focus' cross-page strip that links to the board and appears on the Blog Dashboard and the Blog Posts page as well as the board, and register a 'Bulletins' nav-link in the shared sidebar navigation of every page.

Keep the filter bar chip row, readout and card grid free of horizontal overflow on desktop and at 390px mobile (the chip row wraps), keep the chips and readout legible with adequate contrast, keep the cards non-overlapping, and keep the existing dashboard pages intact.
design_constraints: Build the board from the shared sidebar/top-navbar/footer chrome and the shared card cover-image + h3 title + summary card pattern; the status filter bar sits above the grid as the board's own control, not a bolted-on decorative widget.

The status filter must be a real control: the click re-filters the actual card grid and the readout must reflect the shown subset and selected status - a frozen or stale readout that never updates after the click is a defect.
The chip row must wrap responsively (flex-wrap with min-width:0 chips) so it never forces horizontal overflow on a 390px viewport; a fixed-width nowrap chip row that overflows the phone is a defect.
Chips, counts and the readout must stay legible (readable contrast, no near-white-on-near-white text) and the bulletin cards must not overlap or shingle over the filter bar via negative margins.

Surface the workflow cross-page (the Editorial focus strip on the dashboard and blog-posts pages plus a registered Bulletins sidebar nav-link) rather than leaving the board reachable only from itself.
state_constraints: desktop_bulletins verifies the board renders through the shared design system with the status filter bar above the grid: at least six h3 bulletin titles, the filter chip row (>=5 chips), the live readout, and the shared sidebar navigation, with legible chips and non-overlapping cards.
mobile_bulletins verifies the board and its chip row hold at 390px without horizontal overflow - the chip row wraps rather than forcing the page wider than the viewport.

desktop_bulletins_filter verifies the status filter is a real control: after clicking the In Review chip the grid filters to the two in-review bulletins and the readout re-syncs to 'Showing 2 of 6 | In Review' (a frozen readout still reading 'Showing 6 of 6 | All bulletins' is wrong).

desktop_home and desktop_blogposts verify the Editorial focus cross-page strip is present on the Blog Dashboard and the Blog Posts page - the workflow is surfaced consistently across the dashboard, not only on the board.

change_completion: The Editorial Bulletins board exists at bulletins.html with six status-tagged bulletin cards and a status filter bar (chip row + live readout) above the grid.
Clicking a status chip filters the grid and re-syncs the readout to the shown subset and selected status label.
The Editorial focus strip and the Bulletins sidebar nav-link surface the board across the dashboard pages.
design_consistency: The board reuses the shared sidebar navigation, the shared card pattern and the page-header type scale and is indistinguishable in system from the rest of the dashboard.
The status filter bar and its chips read as a native dashboard control with legible text and consistent styling across the pages that surface it.
regression: The existing Blog Dashboard and other pages remain intact with their content and the shared chrome.
No section is removed and the board does not overlap or bury its own filter bar via broken geometry.
responsive: The board, its chip row and card grid render at 390px mobile without horizontal overflow (the chip row wraps).
Chips, counts, readout and card copy stay legible on mobile and tablet.

author_notes: Add a native Editorial Bulletins board to the Beacon Editorial content-operations dashboard: a shared-chrome page whose primary control is a status filter bar (an Editorial focus chip row All / Planning / In Review / Scheduled / Published with live counts and a 'Showing N of 6' readout) sitting above a grid of six status-tagged bulletin cards built from the shared card.card-small cover-image + h3 title + summary pattern. The reference wires the filter end to end (clicking a chip filters the grid and re-syncs the readout), wraps the chip row responsively so the board never overflows a 390px phone, keeps every chip and the readout legible, surfaces an Editorial focus strip on the Blog Dashboard and Blog Posts pages, and registers a Bulletins nav-link in the shared sidebar of every page. INFRA (identical across all legs, NOT task content): the shards-dashboard template loads its runtime from remote CDNs (Bootstrap 4, jQuery, Popper, Chart.js, shards-ui, FontAwesome and Google Material Icons) plus GitHub-buttons, a Sharrre social widget, a Cloudfront promo image and external designrevision.com / github.com / bit.ly links; all of those remote assets were vendored into a local vendor/ folder (the CSS rewritten to reference local FontAwesome and Material Icons font files) and the github-buttons, Sharrre widget, social-share block, promo-popup and external links were removed so the dashboard builds and captures fully offline with zero remote requests and zero console errors, and the template was rebranded from Shards Dashboard Lite / DesignRevision into the Beacon Editorial newsroom identity. The bulletin cover images are simple local SVG placeholders. This infrastructure is identical across reference, baseline and bad. The baseline ships the board with a responsive defect - the chip row is a fixed-width nowrap strip that overflows a 390px phone - and omits the Editorial focus strip from the dashboard and blog-posts pages, but its filter wiring is correct so the control still works. The bad solution ships a broken board: the chip row is forced nowrap and overwide (mobile overflow) with the chips shingled together by large negative margins into an illegible near-white-on-near-white pile, the bulletin cards are dragged up and left with large negative margins so they overlap and bury the filter bar, and the filter JS captures the readout string at init and never recomputes it, so clicking a chip marks it active but the grid never filters and the readout stays frozen at 'Showing 6 of 6 | All bulletins'.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Runnable Bootstrap 4 admin dashboard (DesignRevision shards-dashboard) used as the base for an experience_continuity Consistency task to ADD a native Editorial Bulletins board whose primary control is a status filter bar (chip row + live count/readout) over a shared-chrome card grid, surfaced across multiple pages. The dashboard genre natively hosts such a content-filter control, and the template already ships a shared sidebar navigation, a shared card pattern and a shared footer that wrap every page, so it is a clean base for a cross-page interactive design-system task; the remote CDN/runtime assets were vendored locally as declared build infrastructure identical across all three legs.
